lawyer:
Mr. Md. Idrisur Rahman with Mr. Md. Shahidullah and Mr. Md. Bodiuzzaman Tapadar, Advocates ------ For the petitioners 
Mr. Mohammad Ali, Advocate ------ For the respondent
parties:
Arun Kumar Sutradhar and another ------ Petitioners
Vs
The Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat Comilla and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Quddus, J.: This Rule Nisi, at the instance of two judgment debtors in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question order dated 26.5.2003 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 1992) issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners to put them in civil prison. 

 2. The petitioners' case in short is that respondent No. 2, Sonali Bank Ltd. as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.182 of 1992 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla against the petitioners and others for recovery of loan amounting to Tk.6,39,608.55 (taka six lac thirty nine thousand six hundred eight take and paisa fifty five) only by selling the mortgaged property and the said suit was decreed on contest against petitioner No: 1 and ex-parte against others by judgment and decree dated 31.5.1994. Thereafter, the decree-holder bank on obtaining the final decree, put the same in execution by, filing Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995. The executing Court after observing the necessary formalities fixed 15.3.1998 for holding auction sale of the mortgaged property. At this stage one Abdul Latif and some others filed Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 1998 under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing the attached property before the executing Court and obtained an order staying the execution proceedings till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case. The decree-holder bank contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection. Ultimately the learned Judge of the executing Court heard the Miscellaneous Case and allowed the same in pint by his judgment and order dated 24.1.2001 releasing a portion of the attached property (vide annexe:B-1 to the writ petition). The decree-holder bank after taking several adjournments, filed an application for amendment of the execution case on 25.7.2002, which the executing Court allowed on 6.5.2003. 

 4. The decree-holder bank as respondent No.2 contests the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the petitioners had fraudulently sold out a' portion of the mortgaged property to others before taking loan from the bank and by concealing the said fact caused huge loss to the bank, but the executing Court without considering these facts had allowed the Miscellaneous Case releasing .98 3/4 acres of land, a portion of the mortgaged property. The respondent's further case is that the executing Court attempted to sell the mortgaged property by fixing a date for holding auction on 15.3.1998, but no bidder participated. After disposal of the Miscellaneous Case, the decree-holder bank filed an application on 26.5.2003 for issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors (herein the petitioners) and the executing Court rightly issued the warrant of arrest to put them in civil prison so that they are compelled for payment of the decretal amount. 

 5. Mr. Md. Idrisur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the impugned order apparently shows that the executing Court had allowed the application for substitution of one of the judgment debtors, but issued warrant of arrest against all to put them in civil prison in violation of section 34 (2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain,2003 (in brief 'the Ain'). The learned Advocate further submits that after the schedule of the execution case was amended on 6.5.2003 releasing a portion of the mortgaged property, no further step was taken by the decree-holder bank for selling the remaining portion and therefore, the provision of section 34 (9) of the Ain was not complied with and without such compliance, issuance of warrant of arrest was in clear violation of law and therefore without lawful authority. 

 8. In order to appreciate the second limb of his argument, we have examined the order sheets of the Artha Decree Execution Case. It appears that an attempt to sell the mortgaged property was made before disposal of the Miscellaneous Case under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But after allowing the Miscellaneous Case and amendment of the schedule of the Execution Case, no subsequent step whatsoever was taken to sell the remaining portion of the mortgaged property. Under the circumstances, we hold that the decree holder bank was required to take step afresh for selling the mortgaged properly after amendment of the schedule of the execution case, failing which, it cannot be said that section 34(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was complied with. It is the cardinal principle of interpretation of statute that any provision of law, which takes away the man's freedom, should be construed strictly. 

 In view of the above, we find substance in the Rule. As a result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 26.5.2003 passed by the Aratha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 1992) issuing warrant of arrest to put the writ petitioners in civil prison is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of or legal effect. 

 9. The executing Court will, however, be at liberty to issue warrant of arrest afresh against the judgment debtors only after due compliance of section 34(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by selling or attempting to sell the mortgaged property (as described in the amended schedule of the execution case), if it is required.
